title: Choosing a spouse
hookLine: four honest reasons people marry, and the one a hadith puts first

cards: A list, written before anyone has met. Steady income? Good family?
Attractive? Gets along with my mother? These days some of that list lives inside apps, as filters you can slide up and down.
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari makes a list like this too, and it's surprisingly frank about it. It doesn't pretend people marry for spiritual reasons alone.
It names four reasons, out loud, and then it points at one of them and says: that one.

teach.b: Here it is, in paraphrase. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: a woman is married for four things: her wealth, her family standing, her beauty, and her religion.
Choose the one with religion, and you will prosper. Then he adds a sharp Arabic phrase, taribat yadak, which literally means may your hands be covered in dust.
Here it works like a nudge: pay attention, get this one right. Notice what the hadith doesn't do. It doesn't call wealth, family or beauty bad.
It names them plainly; it just won't let them sit at the top of the list. Second, character.
A hadith in Jami' at-Tirmidhi speaks to a family receiving a proposal, in paraphrase: if someone comes to you whose religion and character please you, then marry.

The Arabic for character is khuluq: the way a person actually is, on a bad day, when nobody's grading them. Put the two side by side and you have today's line: faith and character first. Third, it runs both ways.
One hadith speaks about choosing a wife, the other about accepting a husband. The same measure falls on both sides. Fourth, what that looks like up close.
Not a title, not how loudly someone talks about religion.

teach.h: WHO SOMEONE IS, NOT WHAT THEY HAVE.
teach.b: It shows in small things: how someone treats the person serving their food, whether they keep a promise that cost them something, how they speak about their parents, whether they keep their prayers on an ordinary weekday.
The filters ask what someone has. These two hadith ask who someone is.

how: Muslims looking for a spouse, and their families, cite the hadith in Bukhari and Tirmidhi to put faith and character ahead of wealth, family standing and looks.

o: choosing for faith and character first, as two hadith teach
picking the wealthiest match so the home is secure
letting parents pick a match by family standing alone

games.q: choosing a spouse — tap the pairs.
p: may your hands be covered in dust
character, the way a person really is

s: the hadith says wealth and beauty don't matter at all
it names them plainly; it just won't put them first.
the hadith in Tirmidhi names character beside religion
if someone whose religion and character please you proposes, marry.
the standard only applies to choosing a wife
Tirmidhi's hadith speaks to the family accepting a husband.

games.q: you're helping a friend think through a match. four things are on the table: wealth, family standing, beauty, religion. which does the hadith say to choose?
o: religion: choose it and you will prosper.
beauty: it keeps a marriage warm.
games.why: choose the one with religion, and you will prosper. the hadith names all four honestly, then puts one first.

practice: Bring to mind someone whose character you trust: not the most impressive person you know, the most dependable. What do they actually do, keep their word, speak kindly of people who aren't in the room?
Then turn it around gently: where does your own character already show like that, and if you pray, ask for good character in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Choosing a spouse. Four reasons people marry, named honestly, and two put first: faith and character. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: character first. Who someone is, before what they have. A new part of the path, begun.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5090 (a woman is married for four things; choose the one with religion; taribat yadak)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1084 (if someone whose religion and character please you proposes, marry)
